command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to create a reminder note for March 27th of this year (2026). They want to remind them about Netflix subscription. We need to use the cmd_controller_execute tool to create a note. But we don't have a specific command for creating notes. We might need to use a generic command like "echo" or "notepad". On Windows, we could use "echo" to write to a file. Or we could use "powershell" to create a scheduled task? But the user just wants a note.

We can create a text file with the note content and maybe schedule a reminder via Task Scheduler. But the user didn't specify how they want to be reminded. Just "make a note".

Simplest: create a text file named "Netflix_Subscription_Reminder.txt" with content "Reminder: Renew Netflix subscription." And maybe add a timestamp.

We can do: `echo Reminder: Renew Netflix subscription > C:\Users\<username>\Documents\Netflix_Subscription_Reminder.txt`. But we don't know username. Could use `%USERPROFILE%`.

So command: `echo Reminder: Renew Netflix subscription > %USERPROFILE%\Documents\Netflix_Subscription_Reminder.txt`

But we also need to set the date. Maybe we can include the date in the file name: "Netflix_Subscription_Reminder_2026-03-27.txt"

Command: `echo Reminder: Renew Netflix subscription > %USERPROFILE%\Documents\Netflix_Subscription_Reminder_2026-03-27.txt`
